sections.h2: Why does Indianapolis property tax run through Marion County?
sections.html:
Indianapolis and Marion County share one government, so the county offices bill and collect the tax for the city. City and county government merged effective January 1, 1970, a move known as Unigov, and Wikipedia notes it added more than 300 square miles and roughly 250,000 residents to the city.

Indianapolis is the state capital and the county seat of Marion County. The 2020 census counted 887,642 residents, the largest city in Indiana. Local government is run by a 25-member city-county council headed by the mayor.

For an owner, the result is simple. You do not pay the city one bill and the county another. The Marion County Treasurer sends one statement, and the Marion County Auditor keeps the records for deductions and tax sales.

sections.h2: Which Marion County offices handle what?
sections.html:
Three county offices touch a typical bill, and each one answers a different question.

OfficeWhat it doesContact
TreasurerBills, takes payments, runs the Stop a Tax Sale process(317) 327-4444, Suite 1001
AuditorHomestead deductions, tax sale redemption and sold parcel questions317.327.4646, Suite W-125
AssessorValues property for taxListed on indy.gov

Both the Treasurer and Auditor sit in the City-County Building at 200 E. Washington St., Indianapolis, IN 46204, and keep hours of 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday through Friday, according to the city's property tax page.

sections.h2: When is Indianapolis property tax due?
sections.html:
Property tax is due twice a year. The 2026 dates posted by Marion County were May 11 and November 10, and a statement with two coupons arrives in April, per the Treasurer's due dates page.

Under state law the standard dates are May 10 and November 10, and a date that lands on a weekend or holiday slides to the next business day. That is why May 10, 2026 became May 11. You may pay the full year on the first date or split it.

The Treasurer extends its counter hours near the fall deadline. For 2026 it opened from 8 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. on November 6, 9 and 10 and closed on Election Day and Veterans Day.

sections.h2: What is the penalty for paying late in Indianapolis?
sections.html:
A late installment costs 5 percent of the unpaid tax if you pay within 30 days and owe nothing older on that property. Wait longer, or carry back taxes on the same parcel, and the penalty is 10 percent.

The state penalty statute, IC 6-1.1-37-10, adds a further 10 percent on unpaid tax after later installment dates, and it counts mailed payments as timely if they are postmarked by the deadline.

Marion County says the date on the U.S. Postal Service postmark counts as the payment date, even when the envelope also carries a business mailing mark.

sections.h2: How can you pay an Indianapolis property tax bill?
sections.html:
You can pay online, by phone, by mail, at a bank, by text or in a drop box. The options come from the Treasurer's payment methods page.

  • Phone: 317.327.4TAX (4829) or 1.888.881.8986, with a $1.95 charge plus a $0.95 convenience fee for e-Check, or $1.95 plus 2.5 percent for cards.
  • Mail: Marion County Treasurer, P.O. Box 6145, Indianapolis, IN 46206-6145, with the parcel number on the check.
  • Bank: First Financial Bank, Merchants Bank of Indiana, Star Financial Bank or Stock Yards Bank & Trust, which may charge fees and take payments only three weeks before the due date.
  • Drop box: first floor of the City-County Building, with payments deposited by midnight on the due date counted on time.

After an online payment it can take up to five business days for the tax bill to show the new balance. Lockbox payments must be checks, not cash.

sections.h2: How do homestead deductions affect an Indianapolis bill?
sections.html:
Homeowners who live in the house can claim two deductions, and the Auditor's Office handles the application. The standard homestead deduction is the lesser of 60 percent of assessed value or $48,000, and a supplemental deduction takes 40 percent of the remaining assessed value, per the Auditor's homestead page.

An application filed by January 15 reflects on that year's bill. Putting the property into a trust, or adding or removing an owner, means filing again.

That last point matters when you sell or inherit a house. A new owner who moves in must apply on their own, and the old owner must tell the office to remove the deductions when they stop living there.

sections.h2: What happens when Indianapolis taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
Marion County places a tax lien on homes with unpaid property tax and sells those liens at an online auction. The 2026 sale was set for October 13 through 16, and the cutoff to stop it was October 8 at 4:30 p.m.

To stop the sale an owner pays unpaid tax, penalties and special assessments, solid waste and stormwater fees, and a $325 tax sale fee. Accepted forms are cash, certified check, cashier's check or money order.

An owner whose parcel sold has one year from the sale date to redeem, or 120 days if it was offered and did not sell. The Auditor's redemption amount tool shows the figure, and our Indiana tax sale guide explains how that number is built.

sections.h2: What should you know about Indianapolis houses before selling?
sections.html:
Indianapolis covers 367.94 square miles, with 361.64 of that land, and its nine townships are Center, Decatur, Franklin, Lawrence, Perry, Pike, Warren, Washington and Wayne. Tax sale lists in Marion County are grouped by township, so the township name on your bill matters.

The mix of housing is wide. Wikipedia lists Broad Ripple, Irvington and University Heights as historic streetcar suburbs, Castleton, Eagledale and Nora as post-war suburbs, and Fountain Square, Old Northside, Lockerbie Square and Fletcher Place among historic districts.

The city averages about 42.4 inches of precipitation a year, with May the wettest month at 5.05 inches, and around 25.9 inches of snow. About 20 days a year have thunderstorms. Older roofs and basements in those wetter months are common repair items before a listing.

Large employers include Eli Lilly with 11,000 workers, Amazon with 9,000, FedEx with 7,000, Rolls-Royce with 4,000 and Allison Transmission with 2,500, and Indianapolis International Airport hosts FedEx Express's National Hub.

sections.h2: How is the unpaid tax handled when you sell?
sections.html:
At closing, the title company asks the Treasurer for a payoff and pays the tax from the seller's proceeds. State law gives the lien for property tax priority over all other liens, so it cannot be skipped.

  • Pull the current bill by parcel number from the Treasurer's site.
  • Ask the Treasurer whether the parcel has a sale date.
  • Check the Auditor's sold parcel finder if you got a notice.

Cash Home Buyers buys Indianapolis houses as-is, with the title company settling back taxes at closing, so a seller does not need to bring cash to the table.

faqs.q: Who do I pay property tax to in Indianapolis?
faqs.a: The Marion County Treasurer. Indianapolis and Marion County share one government, and the Treasurer's Office bills and collects the tax at 200 E. Washington St., Suite 1001.

faqs.q: When are Indianapolis property taxes due?
faqs.a: Twice a year, with 2026 dates of May 11 and November 10. State law sets the dates at May 10 and November 10, moved forward when they fall on a weekend or holiday.

faqs.q: What is the late penalty in Marion County?
faqs.a: Five percent if paid within 30 days and no older tax is owed on the parcel, and 10 percent otherwise.

faqs.q: How do I apply for a homestead deduction?
faqs.a: File with the Marion County Auditor. A filing by January 15 shows on that year's bill, and a title change such as adding an owner or moving the house into a trust requires a new filing.

faqs.q: What is the tax sale administration fee?
faqs.a: For the 2026 Marion County sale, the Treasurer listed a $325 fee on top of unpaid tax, penalties, special assessments and solid waste and stormwater fees.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Indianapolis tax by phone?
faqs.a: Yes. Call 317.327.4TAX (4829) or 1.888.881.8986 with the parcel number. Fees apply to e-Check and card payments.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house in Indianapolis with back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The title company pays the tax from the proceeds at closing, after the Treasurer provides a payoff.
